Consultations
Find out about consultations the council is running and how you can have your say.
Our consultation portal is the place to find all of our active, completed and upcoming consultations, where you can share your views and have your say on what we're doing in your area.
The portal is shared between South Hams and West Devon Council, so please select your area from the tiles on the homepage.
You can also sign up for newsletters and updates about what's happening near you.

pages.text:
Skip to main content
Accessibility information

Shaping Ivybridge Together
At Ivybridge Town Council, we believe every voice matters. We’re proud to represent a diverse and growing community, and we’re committed to doing so fairly, transparently, and inclusively.
Why Your Feedback Matters
We want to ensure that the decisions we make reflect the real needs, ideas, and concerns of the people who live and work here. That means:
Creating more ways for you to share your views
Listening actively to diverse perspectives
Making space for ongoing dialogue, not just one-off consultations
Our Commitment to You
We’re working hard to increase opportunities for insight and engagement, not just around big projects, but in the everyday decisions that shape our town’s future. Whether you have a suggestion, a question, or a concern, your input helps us serve the town better.
Ways to Get Involved
You can now share your views quickly and easily through the contact form below. Any surveys we are running will also be posted to this page, and shared on our social media platforms. Print copies will be available in the town or from the Town Hall.
Use this space to:
Suggest ideas to improve our community
Comment on current issues or proposals
Raise concerns or ask questions
Together, let’s build an Ivybridge that works for everyone.

pages.title: Your Dartmoor - Partnership Plan Consultation
pages.text:
Skip to Main Content
Draft Dartmoor Partnership Plan 2027-2032 – Public Consultation Open Now
Have your say on the future of Dartmoor National Park
We’re consulting on the draft
Dartmoor Partnership Plan 2027–2032
, developed with partners to set out priorities for the future of Dartmoor.
Consultation open: 12
th
October – 22
nd
November 2026
Read the draft Plan
here
Read the Draft Dartmoor Partnership Plan before completing the questionnaire.
Read the draft Plan summary
here
Read a summary of the draft Dartmoor Partnership Plan before completing the questionnaire
Take part in the consultation
here
Prefer to respond another way?
Paper copies are available to view at Parke, Haytor Visitor Centre and Postbridge Visitor Centre.
Help shape the final Plan
The draft Plan has been developed through extensive engagement with communities, partners and stakeholders across Dartmoor. Now we want to hear from you.
We’d like your views on the draft Plan and its proposed priorities, including whether they reflect what matters for Dartmoor and whether there is anything we have missed.
About the Partnership Plan
The Dartmoor Partnership Plan is a shared Plan for the future of Dartmoor, developed and delivered with partners.
It helps turn the Vision for Dartmoor into action, setting out priorities for the next 5 years.
The Plan focuses on seven themes:
Better Response to Climate Change
Better for the Next Generation
Better for Nature & Natural Beauty
Better for Cultural Heritage
Better for Farming & Forestry
Better for People
Better for Business & Communities
What happens next?
We’ll consider responses to the consultation alongside feedback from partners and stakeholders. Your feedback will help shape the final
Dartmoor Partnership Plan 2027–2032
.
Consultation closes 22
nd
November 2026.
Supporting Evidence
The following supporting documents have been prepared to inform the consultation on the draft Dartmoor Partnership Plan 2027–2032:
Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) Environmental Report
– assesses the likely significant environmental effects of the draft Plan and considers how potential adverse effects could be avoided, reduced or mitigated.
Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA)
– considers the potential effects of the draft Plan on internationally important wildlife sites and whether it could affect their conservation objectives.
Non-Technical Summary (NTS)
– provides an accessible overview of the Strategic Environmental Assessment, summarising its key findings and conclusions in plain language.
We welcome your comments on these reports as part of the Partnership Plan consultation, which runs from
12th October to 22nd November 2026
.
Contact us
If you have any questions about the consultation or need help accessing the questionnaire, please contact partnershipplan@dartmoor.gov.uk

pages.title: Community groups in Plymouth - Plymouth Online Directory
pages.text:
Community groups in Plymouth
A community group is normally run by people who live in your local community, and they try to help, support, or provide entertainment.
Community groups can be a great way to meet new people and make friends.
To find out more about how they can help you, please contact them using the phone number, email, or website address they have provided.
Adult Day Centre
Age UK Plymouth runs a welcoming day care service designed for people aged 50 and over in the local area.
Borrow Don't Buy - Plymouth's Library of Things
Borrow Don't Buy is Plymouth's very own Library of Things (LoT). We are a community interest company with the mission of giving you affordable access to the things you need - whilst simultaneously benefitting the Earth.
Claremont Street Neighbourhood Watch
Join the Claremont Street Neighbourhood Watch in Plymouth. Receive local updates, attend community meetings, and help create a safer, friendlier place to live together.
Courtlands School Parent Support Group
We are a support group for parents and meet every Wednesday from 10am to 11.30am. During this time we often have a guest speaker to talk to the group. There is even coffee!
Devon and Cornwall Furniture Reuse Project
The Devon and Cornwall Furniture Reuse Project is a local charity doing big things, we work hard with local people, councils and social housing entities to supply much needed furniture and appliances to people getting back on their feet.
Devon and Cornwall Tamil Sangam
Devon and Cornwall Tamil Sangam is a community group that helps people in Plymouth connect through language, culture, and shared experiences. It supports individuals and families by promoting Tamil identity and building strong local connections.
Disability Football Plymouth Argyle
As part of the Every Player Counts programme funded by Wembley National Stadium Trust, we provide courses and programmes for a wide range of disabilities. Through the project, we aim to improve accessibility, barriers to participation and provide fun, progressive and some competitive programmes for people with disabilities.
Down's Syndrome - Plymouth and Area Support Group
We are a national organisation, committed to improving quality of life for people who have Down's syndrome, promoting their right to be included on a full and equal basis with others.
Dyspraxia Foundation
Dyspraxia is a lifelong condition affecting gross and fine motor coordination in adults and children. Many may experience difficulties with organisational skills, memory, processing speed and, in some cases, speech. The Dyspraxia Foundation is committed to making the teaching and medical professions more aware of dyspraxia; and to spread understanding of how those who have the condition can be helped. The Foundation seeks every opportunity to increase understanding of Dyspraxia.
Eat that Frog
Eat That Frog supports people to identify and overcome their barriers to live a more fulfilled life. Whether you're a teenager or an adult, it's never too late to learn. We provide safe and fun learning environments, tailored around you.
Education Otherwise Association
Education Otherwise is an organisation run by volunteers which provides support and information for families whose children are being educated outside school or for those who are considering home education their children.
Emmanuel Church
Emmanuel Church runs or hosts several community outreach projects including a choir, social responsibility group, Friends of Emmanuel, the Emmanuel Fellowship and a soup run. To get involved or find out current events, look at the website or telephone them directly.
Fun and Freedom Club - Friends and Families of Special Children
Offering young carers a chance to make new friends in a similar situation, it offers lots of fun with weekend clubs, days out and trips away.
Highbury Social Club at Plymouth Highbury Trust
The Highbury Social Club is an evening club for people with varying degrees of learning disabilities. The club is run twice a week, on Tuesday and Friday evenings between the hours of 6.15pm and 8.30pm.
Hope Baptist Church
Hope Baptist Church is a vibrant family church at the heart of Peverell. We hold a range of activities for families, young people and children.

pages.text:
Home
Your Community
Totnes Town Council Community Grants
Following an independent Community Audit, Totnes Town Council (TTC) is updating its community funding model to better support local organisations and projects. Funding will be available through
small grants
to support smaller-scale, time-limited community projects and initiatives; and
core funding
to help provide essential services in the town.
You can apply for a small grant of up to £1,000 at any time. These community grants can support small initiatives and pilot projects, local events, environmental improvements, and community activities that benefit Totnes residents.
The 2026/27 grant allocations and contact email addresses are as follows:
Community Working Group: £5,000 –
clerk@totnestowncouncil.gov.uk
Note: this budget has now been allocated and applications are now closed, see below for details.
Economy Working Group (Event Sponsorship): £2,500 –
economy@totnestowncouncil.gov.uk
Economy Working Group (Business Support): £2,500 –
economy@totnestowncouncil.gov.uk
Environment & Public Realm Working Group: £5,000 –
administrator@totnestowncouncil.gov.uk
Please cc all applications to
reception@totnestowncouncil.gov.uk
For full details on eligibility, terms and conditions, and how to apply, please read the Community Funding Policy and complete the application form below. Applications will initially be reviewed by the relevant Totnes Town Council Working Group.
Small Grants Application Form 2026 – MS Word
82.44KB
·
Mon 27th April 2026
Small Grants Application Form 2026 – PDF
332.79KB
·
Mon 27th April 2026
Community Funding Policy 2026 – PDF
436.19KB
·
Wed 10th June 2026
The simple form above asks for details on how the funds will be spent and the policy which includes details of eligibility and all supporting documents that need to be submitted. Projects that help meet the objectives set out in the Town Council’s 2024-29 Strategy will be prioritised. The grants are funded by a portion of the Council Tax that is collected from Totnes residents. Councillors allocate the available funding at the Council Matters Committee and successful applicants will be informed after this date.
Please note, the next Working Group dates where any initial applications could be considered are:
Economy – 3rd November
Environment – 18th November
This will mean
Mid-September is the earliest date any application can be agreed.
After that it is likely to be September and we expect that to be a significant over subscription for these smaller funding pots. Further conversations about larger grants and strategic funding will be had in due course via committee and we will update as soon as possible.
Community Working Group Grants
– Due to the exceptionally high level of demand, the Community Working Group has agreed to close the Community element of the Grants programme to further applications at this time. This decision was taken because the available budget has been significantly oversubscribed, with the final decision on allocation being taken on 13
th
July by the Council Matters Committee.
We are incredibly grateful for the volume and quality of applications received. It is encouraging to see so many organisations, groups and individuals delivering valuable work for our community. Unfortunately, the level of demand has far exceeded the funds available, and members are tasked with difficult decisions on the applications received already.
However, there is still grant funding available through both the Environment and Public Realm Working Group and the Economy Working Group for projects that align with the priorities of those programmes.
For details of previous grant awards made, see the document below:

Totnes Caring is Recruiting Home Helps
Would you like a worthwhile job based in Totnes?
A role in which you can helps others and make a real difference?
If so, Totnes Caring is currently looking to recruit another home help. Hours are negotiable, but usually about 20-25 per week.
Totnes Caring is a local charity offering help and assistance to older, disabled and vulnerable people living in Totnes and surrounding areas. In particular we offer support to help people live independently at home for as long as possible and not be isolated from the community.
Applicants need to be reliable, personable, caring and hard working to join our busy home help team. Good interpersonal, organisational and communication skills are needed with the ability to work unsupervised. No personal care involved. No weekend or evening work involved.
The home help role involves :
Cleaning and tidying clients home
Making beds and changing bed linen
Assisting with laundry and ironing where necessary
Shopping for housebound clients
Support will be provided by Liz, the Home Help Coordinator.
Previous experience in a similar role would be beneficial, but is not essential as full training will be provided.
Salary: £9.45 per hour plus mileage.
Please apply by emailing Liz Loader liz@totnescaring.org.uk and include your CV.
If you’d like to find out more please contact Liz on the above email or on 01803 865684.
If you you would like to apply or would like more information, please contact:
Contact us on

for more information. or email
info@totnescaring.org.uk
We hope to hear from you very soon.
